# Results — Study 107 (Stochastic-Oscillator) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The recipe: George Lane's
Stochastic Oscillator %K(14)/%D(3); the folk rule is buy when %K crosses above %D while
both are **below 20** (oversold) and sell when %K crosses below %D while both are **above
80** (overbought). Enter at the next day's open, hold for 5 calendar days, pinned against
a **random-direction control** on the same entries. A crossover-only variant (no zone
filter) is included as a secondary framing. As-of **2026-06-13**; daily OHLCV from Yahoo
Finance, 10-year window ending 2026-06-12. Trades pooled across the basket: **n = 1,489**
(zone-filtered) and **n = 6,194** (no zone filter).*

## The honest test — zone-filtered crossover, 5-day hold, gross (cost = 0)

A fixed-horizon forward return (enter at next open, exit at close of day +5) with a
random-direction control on identical entries is the fair test: if the stochastic cross
in an extreme zone points the right way, it beats a coin.

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | skew | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Stochastic zone-cross** | 1,489 | **45.8%** | **−17.19** | −0.27 | **−1.39** |
| Random direction (control) | 1,489 | 51.0% | +6.19 | — | +0.54 |

- The zone-filtered signal earns **−17.19 bps/trade** (HAC *t* = **−1.39**) —
  statistically indistinguishable from zero but directionally *negative*. The coin earns
  **+6.19 bps**, sitting on the right side of zero by chance.
- Delta (cross − random) = **−23.38 bps** — the stochastic is a *worse* entry than a
  fair coin on these 6 instruments over 10 years.
- No instrument carries a real edge. Per-ticker HAC *t*: SPY 0.00, QQQ −0.82,
  IWM +1.03, AAPL −0.30, TSLA −0.55, NVDA −1.75.  Every |*t*| < 2.

## Hold-period sweep (zone-filtered, gross)

The signal shows no directional content at *any* hold window tested:

| Hold period | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 day | 1,489 | 50.8% | −0.17 | −0.04 |
| 3 days | 1,489 | 46.0% | −16.31 | −1.80 |
| **5 days** | **1,489** | **45.8%** | **−17.19** | **−1.39** |
| 10 days | 1,489 | 42.4% | −57.36 | **−2.71** |

At 10-day hold the pooled t-stat crosses −2, but this is driven by a bull-market
tailwind that hurts sell signals: the stochastic fires far more sell signals than buys
in trending instruments (SPY zone signals: 33 buys vs 258 sells, reflecting the secular
uptrend dominating the 10-year window).  This is not an exploitable edge — it is a
buy-and-hold benchmark leak.

## Crossover-only framing (no zone filter, 5-day hold, gross)

Removing the oversold/overbought filter increases trade count six-fold but the signal
remains noise:

| Arm | n | win-rate | mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| All crossovers (no zone filter) | 6,194 | 49.4% | −4.03 | −1.20 |

The zone filter neither adds nor removes a real edge — both framings are noise.

## Cost sweep (zone-filtered, 5-day hold)

The gross edge is already negative, so there is no positive break-even cost:

| Round-trip cost | net mean (bps/trade) | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0.0 bps (gross) | −17.19 | −1.39 |
| 0.5 bps | −17.69 | −1.43 |
| 1.0 bps | −18.19 | −1.47 |
| 2.0 bps | −19.19 | −1.55 |

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery works when there's something to find

On a deterministic synthetic daily tape (`data.synthetic_daily`), the same engine
recovers a stochastic edge **only when mean-reversion is planted** — confirming the rule
is a faithful mean-reversion detector, and that the real tape has no such structure for
it to harvest at this horizon:

| Planted mean-reversion | stoch gross (bps/trade) | beats random? |
|---|--:|:--:|
| 0.00 (martingale) | ≈ 0 (coin) | no |
| +0.15 (mean-reverting) | positive | yes |
| −0.15 (trending) | negative | no (wrong side) |

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** Zone-filtered gross HAC *t* = −1.39 (sign wrong), Δ vs random
  control = −23 bps, every instrument |*t*| < 2.  The stochastic %K/%D crossover in
  oversold/overbought zones carries no real directional information in daily equity data
  over a 10-year window.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** The gross expectancy is already negative; costs deepen a
  loss that starts before they are applied.  No positive break-even cost exists.
- **Beats a coin? — BUSTED.** The coin (random-direction control on identical entries)
  outperforms the stochastic by 23 bps/trade.  The oversold/overbought zone filter
  adds nothing vs no filter — both framings produce noise.
